title: Game deconstruction (.gamestudio/research/*.deconstruction.json)
description: A structured teardown of an existing game in the ontology's terms: core and meta loops, mechanics (mechanic cards), economy, progression, monetization, live-ops, retention hooks, social, notable UX / art / audio, psychology, innovations, weaknesses and lessons, ending in what we borrow. Record only publicly observable or sourced facts; mark inferences as such and date the teardown (as_of) because live games change.

as_of.description: Date the game was observed or the sources were read; live-ops and monetization details go stale quickly.

game.description: Identity of the game being deconstructed.

year.description: Year of global release (state soft-launch years in notes).

core_loop.description: The moment-to-moment loop, as a loop graph (same shape as contract loops).

meta_loops.description: Loops around the core: progression, collection, social, live-ops, monetization.

mechanics.description: Key mechanics as mechanic cards (id and name required; fill what is observable).

currencies.description: Currencies: names, or objects such as {"id": "coins", "kind": "soft", "note": "..."}.

progression.description: Progression structure: tracks, unlock pacing, difficulty pattern.

top_offers.description: Most prominent offers / products and their positioning.

ads.description: Ad usage (placements, pacing), or null if none observed.

liveops.description: Live-ops: event types, cadence, passes, seasons.

retention_hooks.description: Mechanisms that bring players back (streaks, timers, social obligations, collections).

social.description: Social features: teams, gifting, leaderboards, PvP.

psychology.description: Psychological principles the design leans on (e.g. goal-gradient effect, loss aversion), each tied to the feature that uses it.

innovations.description: What the game did first or better than its genre.

weaknesses.description: Weaknesses and player complaints; openings for competitors.

lessons.description: General lessons, stated as reusable rules.

borrow_for_us.description: Concrete, transformed borrowings for our project (what, and how we change it).

sources.description: URLs backing the factual claims (store pages, developer talks, reputable analyses).
